name: Goodluck India Ltd
tagline: Legacy working-capital-heavy steel/engineering converter with a fast-scaling 155mm artillery-shell subsidiary -- the defence mix inflection is now visible in consolidated numbers (Q1 FY27 rev +31%, EBITDA +46%, PAT +67%), but the 400k-shell capacity expansion has slipped 6-9 months and the subsidiary raised outside equity, leaving parent-shareholder value capture unresolved
business_overview: Goodluck India is a diversified engineering conglomerate (steel tubes, pipes, forgings, fabricated structures) that has entered defense manufacturing through subsidiary Goodluck Defence & Aerospace, producing 155mm artillery shells under an Arms Act industrial license, with recent export certification and order wins.

fundamentals_narrative: The base steel/engineering business is a commoditised, working-capital-heavy converter -- FY26 consolidated revenue grew only 4.1% though EBITDA rose ~21% (margin 8.75% -> 10.16%) and PAT to owners was Rs 182.6 Cr (+10.2%). ROCE is ~15%, borrowings rose 22% in FY26 (finance costs +32%), and cash conversion is structurally weak (FY24 operating cash flow was negative). The signal is the Defence & Aerospace subsidiary: a 155mm artillery-shell facility inaugurated Oct-2025 at 30-38% EBITDA margin (roughly triple the base), Rs 300+ Cr of orders in hand, export certification with a first overseas dispatch, and FY27 guidance of Rs 300-350 Cr revenue at 30-35% margin. Q1 FY27 already carried this through to consolidated numbers (revenue +31%, EBITDA +46%, PAT +67%). Two overhangs remain live: (1) the 400k-shell capacity expansion (~Rs 400-500 Cr) has slipped 6-9 months -- commissioning now Q4 FY27, commercialisation Q4 FY28; and (2) the subsidiary raised Rs 285 Cr from non-promoter investors at Rs 375/share, cutting the parent's stake from 100% to ~81.5%, with a Rs 275 Cr corporate guarantee at the parent -- management has been vague about the restructuring / separate-listing plan and was grilled on it in the concall. Promoter holding in Goodluck India slipped from ~56.4% to ~54.0% over the year.
technical_read: Not checked -- the defense-subsidiary margin-mix catalyst and its governance overhang were the decisive factors.

verdict_headline: Real defence margin-mix inflection now visible in consolidated numbers, held at Medium / 10x-in-2-3-years because a 6-9 month capacity slip and an unresolved subsidiary capital-structure question cap how much value reaches parent shareholders
verdict_reasoning: The defence pivot is a genuine, specific, recent-quarter catalyst that has now flowed into consolidated P&L (Q1 FY27 EBITDA +46%, PAT +67%), with real export certification, orders in hand and a facility running at ~38% EBITDA margin. four_box scores 3.0 (tailwind + tam yes; moat + valuation weak) so the 10x-in-2-3-years label is permitted.

Conviction held at Medium, not raised: (a) the 400k-shell capacity expansion has slipped 6-9 months, pushing commercialisation to Q4 FY28; (b) the subsidiary raised Rs 285 Cr from non-promoter investors at Rs 375/share, cutting the parent's stake to ~81.5%, and management gave only vague answers on the restructuring / listing plan despite a Rs 275 Cr corporate guarantee at the parent. How much of the defence upside accrues to Goodluck India minorities is genuinely unclear.

Red-flag check: none. The subsidiary capital-structure vagueness and rising leverage are governance / capital-allocation drags that cap conviction but do not meet AVOID / HIGH CAUTION / EXCLUDE definitions. Promoter holding down ~2.4pp YoY is a watch-item.

Re-check on: (a) defence capacity commissioning vs the Q4 FY27 target, (b) any concrete disclosure on the subsidiary's listing / restructuring structure, (c) base-business leverage and cash conversion, (d) defence sub tracking to the Rs 300-350 Cr FY27 guide.

four_box.note: Defence 155mm artillery-shell export certification + capacity roadmap (150k->400k) from a small base supports tailwind/tam; the export-certification / Arms Act barrier is a real but unproven-at-volume moat (weak); at consol P/E ~26x on a ~15% ROCE base the defence optionality is partly priced -- valuation weak. Score 3.0 keeps 10x-in-2-3-years permitted; conviction held at Medium because the capacity expansion slipped 6-9 months and the subsidiary capital structure / parent-minority value capture is unresolved.
